posts.cooked:
This has got to be winnable ... please show me how.

 

Visionary, Absolute Zero, Ra, and Haka (in that order) vs The Chairman in Rook City

 

Had this come up on random. Tried it four times before I ran out of time. Only got The Chairman to flip once. Twice I used Brain Burn to bury most of the Thugs back in the deck, but it was too little too late in both cases. Yes, I tried using Savage Mana to grab Villain targets, but lost so many hit points setting it up that I was just about dead before I got more than a couple of them. I got Twist the Ether on The Operative a couple of times, but too many other things went wrong for it to matter much.

 

I tried just focusing on The Operative, since I had some pretty consistent damage dealing, but she healed most of the damage I did. I tried just keeping up with the underbosses and thugs, but fell behind and then got hit with a prison break anyway. I tried doing everything I could to avoid playing extra villain cards, but fell behind because of not being able to play hero cards a lot (Visionary and AZ couldn't take out the necessary Thug w/ their base power), and got punished by leaving the relevant environment card in play (Scum & Villainy, maybe?).

 

Ugh.

posts.name: danmarshall14
posts.cooked:
Killswitch:

On paper, it looks fantastic. Visionary brings to the table her TtE on AZ to grant any desired effect at a given time, and protects against the environment with her Mass Levitation. Ra is the heavy hitter, and Haka shuts down the grave, deals massave rounds of damage and nulls it with Ground Pound.I'll definitely have to try this when I get home.

The problem is that Mass Levitation rarely helps against Rook City since Rook City itself rarely damages the players (except for the falling statues and gunmen).  Most of the time, Rook City is just beefing up the villain damage (blighted streets) or making you play more Villain deck cards.  Even for Scum and Villainy, the damage source is the Villain, so Mass Levitation does nothing.  

Twist the Ether on Absolute Zero though is quite nasty.  Or better yet, put it on The Operative and kill her minions with zero guilt as all the damage goes to Absolute Zero and heals him, keeping him as the highest HP hero.

And all the other pieces add up just fine.  AZ, Ra, and Haka have enough damage to control the villain targets.  And once the Chairman flips, Ground Pound can buy you a full turn of free damage against retaliations.

posts.cooked:
I beat it first try, but I had a fantastic starting hand.

 

Chairman's opening:  Prison Break & Deputy

Amongst my weapondry:  Brain Burn, Prophetic Vision, Precognition, Savage Mana, Taiaha...

 

I Brain Burned first thing, and then had Haka eat all the underbosses.  Then I puttered around for a while setting up with Twist the Ethers on the Chairman & Operative, Imbued Fire, Flesh of the Sun God, etc.  Then Haka of Battle + Savage Mana to drop the Operative almost to dead and flip the Chairman, and pound until dead.

 

A first turn Brain Burn really feels like cheating against the Chairman.
